reason: The kidney blood sample is approaching a filter, and the nephron includes that filter, so they are a clear starting pair.
expectation: The nephron will filter some fluid and dissolved substances from the blood.

effect: The filter put fluid and small substances into the tubule while keeping blood cells and most proteins in the blood. Next, the useful substances need to be recovered.
reaction: The picture made the separation clear.
reason: The transporters are in the tubule wall beside blood, so they look suited to recovering substances from the filtered sample.
expectation: Some useful dissolved substances will move from the tubule back toward the blood.

effect: The transporters returned glucose and other useful substances toward the blood. Water recovery looks like the next step.
reaction: It is useful to see that filtering does not mean losing all the glucose.
reason: The water-permeable tubule picture shows water moving toward blood, matching the recovery goal.
expectation: Some water will return from the tubule to the blood, leaving a more concentrated remaining fluid.

effect: Water returned to the blood while wastes stayed in the tubule. The remaining fluid can now follow the urinary drainage route.
reaction: The separate recovery steps make the process easier to follow.
reason: The urinary drainage leads from the kidney toward the bladder, matching the goal of following the remaining fluid to urine.
expectation: The remaining fluid will leave the tubule as urine and enter the drainage route.

effect: The remaining fluid became urine and travelled through a ureter to the bladder. The filtering goal is complete; the urinary organs still need connecting to the body.
reaction: Seeing the full route to the bladder is satisfying.
reason: The kidney pair has a named ureter slot, and the ureters connect kidneys to the bladder.
expectation: The ureters will be fitted to the kidneys.

effect: The ureters are fitted to the kidneys; the bladder slot remains.
reason: The bladder is the remaining named slot, and the ureters lead to it.
expectation: The bladder will be fitted to the kidney pair and ureters.

effect: The kidneys, ureters and bladder are now connected; the urinary organs still need to join the body.
reaction: The route from kidneys to bladder is clear.
reason: The remaining goal is to connect the urinary organs to the body, and these are the two matching structures.
expectation: The urinary organs will connect to the body and its blood supply.

effect: The urinary organs are connected to the body's circulation, completing both goals.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the kidney route joined to the whole body.

mostWorthwhile.text: Recovering glucose after filtering was most worthwhile: it showed that useful substances enter the tubule too, rather than the filter removing only waste.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the ureters and bladder was clear but fairly predictable because the slots named both parts.

surprise.text: I was surprised that almost all filtered glucose is normally recovered in healthy kidneys.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; the pictures and named slots made the connections understandable.

continue.text: I might continue if the next chapter connects another system to the body. This chapter made the kidney process clear, though the organ-fitting steps were predictable.
